$comment: Branch protection on `main` as GitHub enforces it (GET repos/basiltt/CandleViewer/branches/main/protection, 2026-10-18). Every setting the API reports is declared here, because a full PUT replaces the whole object. scripts/check_branch_protection_drift.py compares each one with the live state and proves that `ci-required` judges every CONSTITUTION.md C-9.1 check (scripts/check_required_check_reconciliation.py). Its weekly run (governance-drift.yml) has not compared anything yet: the GH_BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN secret it reads is not provisioned (docs/ci-runbook.md), so it stops at 'token not found'. Owner item: add that secret, a fine-grained token for this repository with read-only Administration access. Nothing requires the `governance` workflow, which runs the GOV-00x checks and these scripts' tests on every PR. Owner item: add {"context": "governance", "app_id": 15368} to required_status_checks.checks (it must then report on merge_group too once #3433 queues PRs), or make it a lane `ci-required` judges. scripts/apply_branch_protection.py only prints its changes unless given --apply. It refuses unknown keys and refuses a change that weakens the live protection unless given --allow-weaken. `$` keys are notes. `branch` and `pending_checks` are never sent or compared. There is no `merge_queue` block (a ruleset): add it once the owner turns the queue on after #3433. $deviations names each setting that falls short of the Constitution and the owner item that closes it.

$deviations.required_status_checks: C-9.1 requires its checks on `main` branch protection, by names that match the job names in .github/workflows/. GitHub requires one check, `ci-required` from GitHub Actions (app 15368): the ADR-0013 rule 2 resolver, which fails unless every applicable lane passed. The reconciliation proves that every C-9.1 check except pending_checks is a lane it judges, mapping the names that differ. Owner item, one of: amend C-9.1 to say its checks are required through `ci-required`; or keep C-9.1 as written, give each C-9.1 name a job that always reports its lane's result (as `architecture` does for the py lane), and require those names here. CONSTITUTION.md is unchanged. strict is false, so a PR can merge green against an older `main`. Owner item: turn on GitHub's merge queue once #3433 lands (01-sdlc-and-branching.md section 7), or set strict to true until then.
$deviations.required_pull_request_reviews: C-4.1, C-10.1 and ADR-0013 rule 1 expect GitHub to require reviews and dismiss stale approvals. The agents share the owner's GitHub account, and GitHub does not count an author's own approval, so any count above 0 would block every merge while enforce_admins is true. Instead, C-10.1's two independent reviews are recorded on the PR and checked against the head commit by the delivery orchestrator's merge guard. Owner item: amend C-4.1 to name that guard, or give reviewers their own accounts, then set 2 approvals, code-owner review, last-push approval and stale-review dismissal.
$deviations.required_conversation_resolution: C-10.7 and 01-sdlc-and-branching.md section 6.1 say an unresolved review thread blocks merge. GitHub does not enforce that today. Owner item: set this to true.

pending_checks.$comment: C-9.1 checks that nothing enforces yet: neither `ci-required` nor a required check of their own. Read only by the reconciliation, which fails on a C-9.1 check that is neither enforced nor listed here, and on an entry that is enforced now.
pending_checks.bundle-size: No PR workflow runs size-limit or scripts/check-bundle-size-regression.mjs. #3080 wires it into CI, in a lane that `ci-required` judges.
pending_checks.pr-metadata: pr-metadata.yml is a separate workflow so that title, body and label edits re-run it, which means `ci-required` cannot judge it. Owner item (#2280): add {"context": "pr-metadata", "app_id": 15368} to required_status_checks.checks, after #3433 makes it report on merge_group if the queue comes first.
